title: Hawthorn Bend — A Tour of the Map

success_criteria.description: All four districts are in use and every precinct is assigned.
All four districts have roughly equal population (within 10%).

character.name: Tutorial Guide
character.motivation: Welcome to Hawthorn Bend. This map shows every kind of terrain feature that you will see in the game.

intro_slides.heading: Reading the Map
intro_slides.body:
Maps can include geographic features alongside the precincts you draw districts from.

- **Mountains** (grey tiles, northwest) — not assignable. Adjacent precincts are foothills with a soft grey fringe.
- **Sea** (dark blue tiles, south) — not assignable. Adjacent precincts are coast with a blue shoreline.
- **Lake** (aqua tile, centre) — not assignable. Adjacent precincts show a teal lakeside fringe.
- **River** (teal line) — flows from the mountain area, through the lake, and down to the sea.

intro_slides.heading: Geography is Cosmetic
intro_slides.body:
These features are visual: they show what the region looks like, but **they do not constrain district-drawing**.

Real redistricting often uses rivers and mountains as district boundaries — but that is because of political choices (state lines, county lines, historical municipal limits) that happen to follow geography, not because geography is a physical barrier. A district can cross a river or lake if the people on both sides share a community.

The initial map divides the region into four sectors. It is already a valid plan.

intro_slides.heading: Try It Out
intro_slides.body:
Click **Submit Map** to evaluate the starting districts. You can also repaint districts to experiment — drag across hexes to assign them, click district buttons to switch which district you are drawing.

When you are done exploring, move on to the educational campaign.

narrative.objective: Look around the map at the terrain features. Submit the initial four-district map, or repaint to experiment.
